newsitem.title: UK: Nat Power "pleased" with pensions ruling.
newsitem.headline: Nat Power "pleased" with pensions ruling.

text.p: British electricity generator National Power Plc said on Tuesday it was "pleased" with a British court decision in its favour over use of pension surpluses to fund redundancy payments.

Mr Justice Robert Walker allowed an appeal by transmission company National Grid Group Plc against a decision by Britain's pensions ombudsman that it should return 43 million stg and ruled that arrangements made by National Power had been valid and effective.
National Power had sought clarification over its position after the pensions ombudsman ruled on National Grid's use of pension surpluses.
It could have been asked to pay back as much as 200 million stg.
The judge said the ombudsman's decision had been based on "a misunderstanding of the terms of the scheme and of the employers' duties in dealing with surplus."
He gave the two National Grid employees who had brought the case leave to appeal.
